headline: Post-quantum enrollment fix, sync and transfer hardening, blamejs v0.14.10
summary: Restores the post-quantum TLS posture on the enrollment handshake, stops the sync loop from stalling after a rejected server event, hardens HTTP-client shutdown and interrupted transfers, reclaims orphaned download temp files from nested directories, and advances the vendored framework to v0.14.10.

items.title: Enrollment handshake advertises the post-quantum TLS posture
items.body: First-contact enrollment negotiated Node's default elliptic curves over TLS 1.2 instead of the post-quantum group preference every other request uses, because it built a bare HTTPS agent that bypassed the transport's posture injection. Against a server that enforces the post-quantum gate, enrollment was rejected at the TLS handshake. The enrollment client now offers the same ML-KEM hybrid groups and pins TLS 1.3, so enrollment succeeds against a hardened server; self-signed certificates are still accepted at first contact, with the server-issued client certificate and CA pin taking over immediately after.

items.title: Sync no longer stalls after a rejected server event
items.body: If a server change event at the tip of the change log was rejected by the client's path-traversal guard, the sync cursor stopped advancing, and every reconnect replayed the same blocked event ahead of newer ones — silently halting further sync. Rejected events now advance the cursor so later changes continue to apply and catch-up completes.

items.title: Hardened HTTP-client shutdown and interrupted transfers
items.body: Three lifecycle defects are fixed: a buffered rename-detection delete could fire after shutdown against a torn-down client and surface as an unhandled rejection; an aborted download response left its file handle open and its partial temp file behind; and reloading client certificates after a CA rotation aborted any in-flight upload or download. Pending deletes are now cancelled on shutdown, an interrupted download cleans up and rejects, and the previous connection pool drains across a credential swap instead of being destroyed mid-transfer.

items.title: Interrupted-download temp files reclaimed from subdirectories
items.body: The startup sweep that removes leftover download temp files only scanned the sync-folder root, so a temp left inside a nested directory accumulated indefinitely. The sweep now recurses into subdirectories and matches only the downloader's exact temp-file suffix, so a user file that merely contains that token in its name is never removed.

items.title: Failure messages from newer servers surface correctly
items.body: Enrollment and certificate-renewal failures now read the server's structured error detail field, falling back to the legacy field, so the message shown to the operator matches what a current server returns instead of a generic status line.

items.title: Vendored blamejs refreshed to v0.14.10
items.body: The bundled framework advances from v0.11.33 to v0.14.10. The wire-layer surfaces this client consumes — the WebSocket client, the HTTP client and its per-session encryption envelope, the post-quantum TLS agent, and the JSON parser — carry no API or behaviour change across the gap, and the vendored cryptographic bundles are byte-identical, so the runtime behaviour of the binary is unchanged. The release SBOM gains the @noble/curves bundle the framework now ships.
